entries.answer_gold: Any color. Blood Moon operates in the type-changing layer which is applied before the ability adding and removing layer. Sunlit Marsh is a Mountain, with the additional ability "{T}: Add one mana of any color.".

entries.question: Avery enchants their [Hall] with [Unbridled Growth]. Next turn, Nickolas casts [Blood Moon]. What colors of mana can Hall tap for?
entries.reason: The candidate concludes Hall taps only for red, which contradicts the reference ruling that Hall can tap for any color because Unbridled Growth's granted ability remains effective.
entries.answer:
Only red. After Nickolas's Blood Moon resolves, Avery's Hall can tap only for {R}.

Why: Blood Moon says "Nonbasic lands are Mountains," and per Blood Moon ruling #2 nonbasic lands lose any other land types and abilities they had and gain the type Mountain plus "{T}: Add {R}." Hall is a nonbasic land, so in the type-changing layer it becomes a Mountain, and in the ability layer it loses everything it had — its printed "{T}: Add {R} or {W}", its "enters tapped" ability, and its {4},{T} Investigate ability.

The ability Unbridled Growth grants ("{T}: Add one mana of any color") is also stripped. Unbridled Growth was attached first, so its granted ability has the earlier timestamp; Blood Moon's ability-removal is applied afterward in the same layer and removes abilities granted by earlier-timestamped effects. Unbridled Growth itself stays on the battlefield (Hall is still a land, so it's still a legal enchant target) and you can still sacrifice it to draw a card — but while Blood Moon is out, the aura grants nothing.

Hall then has the intrinsic Mountain ability from rule 305.6: "{T}: Add {R}" (for Mountains the mana symbol is {R}). Note {R} is specifically red mana, not generic and not colorless (rules 107.4a, 106.1a).

Timing note: this assumes Blood Moon resolved after Unbridled Growth was already attached, as stated. If Unbridled Growth were instead attached *after* Blood Moon was already on the battlefield, the aura's granted ability would have the later timestamp and would survive — Hall would then tap for {R} (from Mountain) or for one mana of any color.

This works the same at any player count; nothing here depends on the number of opponents.

entries.question: What layer does [Grand Abolisher]'s "During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments." ability apply in?
entries.reason: Both answers state the ability doesn't apply in any layer because it doesn't change object characteristics and is a static ability that creates a continuous effect forbidding certain actions.
entries.answer:
Grand Abolisher's ability doesn't apply in any layer at all. The layer system of rule 613 exists only to determine the values of an object's characteristics — copiable values, control, text, types, colors, abilities, power/toughness (see [613.1], [613.1a], [613.1b], [613.1f]). Grand Abolisher's ability changes no characteristic of any object; it is a static ability generating a continuous effect that says something can't happen (your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments during your turn).

Such "can't happen" effects are not replacement effects and are not characteristic-modifying effects; they simply forbid the action ([614.17]), and a player can't even begin to activate an ability that's prohibited ([602.5]). Because there's nothing to layer, questions of timestamp order ([613.7]) or dependency ([613.8]) don't arise either — if two such prohibitions exist, both simply apply.

Note also that Grand Abolisher only stops activated abilities of artifacts, creatures, and enchantments on the battlefield, not abilities activated from other zones such as cycling ([Grand Abolisher ruling #1]), and it doesn't affect triggered or static abilities at all ([Grand Abolisher ruling #0]). This is the same whether you're in a two-player game or a multiplayer one — it applies to each of your opponents during your turn.

entries.answer_gold: Because Grand Abolisher's ability doesn't change the characteristics of any objects, it doesn't apply in any layer. Instead it's a static ability that generates a continuous effect that modifies the rules of the game.
